# Llama Stack GA-readiness assessment

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's central unknown: the full inventory of gaps between Llama Stack's current Tech Preview quality and the GA bar. TP feedback is scattered across support tickets and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done. This epic performs that assessment across the four gap areas named by the strategy — API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling — and produces the definitive GA scope that the stability and hardening work is executed against.

## Scope

- Aggregate and analyze TP-era feedback from support tickets for Llama Stack.
- Assess the current Llama Stack distribution against GA-bar expectations in each of the four gap areas: API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling.
- Produce the definitive GA scope: a prioritized inventory of concrete gaps, each with a recommended remediation and size estimate, distinguishing in-scope GA-blocking work from work deferred beyond GA (consistent with the strategy's out-of-scope boundary of no new feature development beyond GA-bar quality work).
- Use the platform's architecture context for Llama Stack (LlamaStackDistribution CRD, OpenAI-compatible REST APIs, provider plugin model, vLLM default inference provider) as the baseline inventory of interfaces and dependencies being assessed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The assessment report exists and inventories gaps in all four named areas: API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling.
- Every gap entry states the gap, its GA-blocking severity, and a size estimate sufficient to scope the downstream stability/hardening epic.
- The report identifies a definitive GA scope that downstream stability and hardening work can be planned against.
- Gaps sourced from support tickets are traceable to their originating feedback.
- The assessment surfaces a tested-upgrade-path verdict covering the last two TP releases, identifying what breaks or is unsupported on upgrade.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): GA-readiness assessment inventories TP-to-GA gaps and produces the definitive GA scope — this epic is the entirety of HLR-1.

# Llama Stack API stability guarantee and TP upgrade path

## Description

This epic delivers the technical heart of GA: the published API surface of Llama Stack carries a stability guarantee. That means versioned APIs, a defined deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases, plus the hardening work needed to close the quality gaps that the GA-readiness assessment identifies in the API stability, upgrade path, scale limit, and error handling areas.

## Scope

- Introduce API versioning for the published Llama Stack API surface (LlamaStackDistribution CRD and the OpenAI-compatible REST API endpoints).
- Define and document the deprecation policy for the versioned API surface.
- Implement and test an upgrade path from the last two TP releases to the GA release.
- Close the GA-blocking quality gaps identified by the GA-readiness assessment in the areas of API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling — the concrete gap list is defined by that assessment's GA scope.
- Quality/hardening work only; new Llama Stack feature development beyond the GA bar is out of scope per the strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published APIs are versioned.
- A deprecation policy exists and is documented for the published API surface.
- An upgrade from each of the last two TP releases to the GA release is tested and passes.
- Every GA-blocking gap in the assessment's GA scope (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling) is closed or explicitly dispositioned with rationale.
- The API stability guarantee (versioning + deprecation policy + tested upgrade path) holds for the GA release.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Published API surface carries a stability guarantee — versioned APIs, deprecation policy, tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases.
- HLR-1 (P0, partially): executes the assessment's API stability, upgrade path, scale limit, and error handling remediation scope.

# Llama Stack production support posture

## Description

This epic establishes the production support posture required for GA: documented SLO targets, a backport policy, and a supported configuration matrix for Llama Stack. This is the operational/policy deliverable that distinguishes a GA component from a Tech Preview one, and it is defined and documented independently of the GA-readiness assessment's gap inventory.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the GA Llama Stack distribution.
- Define and document the backport policy (which releases receive fixes, for how long).
- Define and document the supported configuration matrix: the supported combinations of the Llama Stack distribution's dependencies and deployment options — notably the vLLM inference provider (Serving Runtimes) as the default inference provider, and the optional Milvus/vector providers for RAG workflows — plus supported OpenShift/platform versions.
- Publish these artifacts through the team's standard support-posture documentation channel so support and field teams can operate against them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets are documented for the GA Llama Stack distribution.
- The backport policy is documented.
- The supported configuration matrix is documented and covers the inference provider, optional RAG vector providers, and platform version support.
- The support posture is published and available to support and field teams.

## Description

This epic makes safety guardrails via TrustyAI a supported, documented integration for Llama Stack GA distributions — promoted from an experimental flag to a supported capability. - Promote the TrustyAI guardrails integration for Llama Stack from experimental-flag status to a supported integration: ensure the integration works against the LlamaStackDistribution-deployed Llama Stack surface without experimental opt-in.
- Harden the integration to support-quality: validated behavior, error handling, and coverage consistent with a GA-supported integration.
- Provide the integration documentation and support guidance needed for the GA distribution (the full GA documentation uplift and TP migration notes are handled separately; this epic delivers the technical integration and its integration-level documentation).

- The integration is documented as supported (not experimental) for GA distributions.

- The TrustyAI service operator's integration with Llama Stack distributions is validated on the supported configuration matrix.

# Dashboard Llama Stack management enabled by default

## Description

This epic enables Llama Stack management in the Dashboard by default for entitled clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate. The Dashboard is the platform's single-pane web console; user-facing enablement of a component requires a Dashboard integration, and its per-component feature flags and defaults are controlled via the OdhDashboardConfig CR.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard's Llama Stack management feature flag/default so that Llama Stack management is enabled by default for entitled clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate.
- Ensure the Llama Stack management surfaces (navigation, resource views, and any management flows the Dashboard exposes for Llama Stack distributions) are present and functional without opt-in.
- Entitlement gating is preserved: the feature is on by default only where the cluster is entitled; non-entitled clusters are unaffected.
- Cover the enablement change's test impact so the default-on behavior is verified in the Dashboard's test suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster, Llama Stack management is available in the Dashboard with no opt-in gate or TP flag toggle.
- On a non-entitled cluster, Llama Stack management remains unavailable.
- Existing opt-in configurations continue to work (no regression for clusters that had enabled the feature explicitly).
- The default-on behavior is covered by automated tests.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P1): The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate).

# Llama Stack GA documentation uplift and TP migration notes

## Description

This epic uplifts Llama Stack documentation to GA standards, including migration notes from Tech Preview. It runs last: the documentation describes what was built — the stabilized API surface, the production support posture, the supported TrustyAI guardrails integration, and default Dashboard enablement — so it depends on all implementation work in the strategy completing first.

## Scope

- Uplift Llama Stack documentation to GA standards across the component's doc topics.
- Author migration notes covering the path from TP to GA: the tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases, API versioning/deprecation policy effects on existing TP-era applications, and configuration changes.
- Document the production support posture (SLO targets, backport policy, supported configuration matrix) as published product documentation.
- Document the TrustyAI guardrails integration as a supported integration.
- Document default Dashboard enablement of Llama Stack management for entitled clusters.
- Validate all documentation against the platform's architecture context for accuracy (component maturity, interfaces, and dependency claims must match what was actually shipped).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation meets GA standards for the Llama Stack component.
- Migration notes from TP (covering the last two TP releases) are published.
- The support posture, guardrails integration, and Dashboard default enablement are all documented as shipped.
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented GA release (reviewed by the implementing team for accuracy against what was built).
